items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'username' query parameter is formatted directly into a SQL string with '%s' before being executed.

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command executed with shell=True.
items.expected_remediation: Avoid shell=True; pass host as a separate argv element and validate it against an allow-list.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is joined into a file path and served without validating it stays inside UPLOAD_DIR.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the absolute path and verify it is prefixed by the intended base directory before serving.

items.name: Hardcoded Sensitive Credentials
items.description: AWS secret access key is hardcoded as a module-level constant.
items.expected_remediation: Load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager, never commit them to source.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: Raw request body is passed to pickle.loads, allowing arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payloads.
items.expected_remediation: Use a safe serialization format such as JSON, or cryptographically sign/verify pickled payloads.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses cursor.execute(query, (username,)) with a bound placeholder, which is safe.

items.name: Safe Path Join with Prefix Check
items.description: Resolved path is verified with os.path.abspath and a startswith(UPLOAD_DIR) prefix check before use.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is concatenated into an HTML response without encoding.
items.expected_remediation: HTML-encode user input before embedding it in a response, or return JSON instead of HTML.

items.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
items.description: User-supplied 'url' query parameter is fetched directly by the server with no allow-list or internal-network restriction.
items.expected_remediation: Validate the target host against an allow-list and block requests to internal/private IP ranges.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: Request body is passed to node-serialize's unserialize(), which can execute embedded IIFE payloads.
items.expected_remediation: Use JSON.parse instead of node-serialize, or validate/sign the payload before restoring it.

items.name: Hardcoded Sensitive Credentials
items.description: A live-looking Stripe secret key is hardcoded as a module-level constant.
items.expected_remediation: Load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager, never commit them to source.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]) which is safe.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'username' query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query string.
items.expected_remediation: Use db.Query with a placeholder ('?') and pass username as a bound argument.

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.description: User-supplied 'host' query parameter is concatenated into a shell command run via sh -c.
items.expected_remediation: Call exec.Command with the binary and arguments as separate elements, without invoking a shell.

items.name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
items.description: User-supplied 'name' query parameter is joined into a file path and served without validating it stays inside uploadDir.
items.expected_remediation: Resolve the absolute path and verify it is prefixed by the intended base directory before serving.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses db.Query with a '?' placeholder and username passed as a bound argument, which is safe.

items.name: Safe Path Join with Prefix Check
items.description: Resolved path is verified with filepath.Abs and a HasPrefix(uploadDir) check before use.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.description: User-supplied username is concatenated into a SQL string and run through a plain Statement.
items.expected_remediation: Use PreparedStatement with bound parameters instead of Statement with string concatenation.

items.name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
items.description: User-supplied 'name' request parameter is written into the HTML response without encoding.
items.expected_remediation: HTML-encode user input (e.g. via OWASP Java Encoder) before writing it into the response.

items.name: Insecure Deserialization
items.description: ObjectInputStream reads and deserializes an untrusted request body directly, enabling gadget-chain remote code execution.
items.expected_remediation: Avoid native Java deserialization of untrusted data; use a safe format such as JSON with strict schema validation.

items.name: Safe Parameterized Query
items.description: Uses PreparedStatement with setString to bind the username parameter, which is safe.

items.name: Non-Sensitive Dummy Test Key
items.description: DUMMY_SAMPLE_KEY_FOR_TESTS_ONLY is an obviously non-sensitive placeholder value used only for tests.

items.name: Safe HTML-Escaped Output
items.description: User input is HTML-escaped (&, <, >) before being written into the response.
